spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m4p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Workers, CAP, MaxTasks

VARIABLES queue, assigned, done, nextTask

FREE == 0
vars == <<queue, assigned, done, nextTask>>

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ assigned = [w \in Workers |-> FREE]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ nextTask = 1

Submit ==
    /\ nextTask <= MaxTasks
    /\ Len(queue) < CAP
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, nextTask)
    /\ nextTask' = nextTask + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assigned, done>>

Dispatch ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ \E w \in Workers :
         /\ assigned[w] = FREE
         /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![w] = Head(queue)]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, nextTask>>

Complete ==
    /\ \E w \in Workers :
         /\ assigned[w] # FREE
         /\ done' = done \cup {assigned[w]}
         /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![w] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, nextTask>>

Release ==
    /\ Len(queue) < CAP
    /\ \E w \in Workers :
         /\ assigned[w] # FREE
         /\ queue' = Append(queue, assigned[w])
         /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![w] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, nextTask>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ nextTask > MaxTasks
    /\ Len(queue) = 0
    /\ \A w \in Workers : assigned[w] = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Submit \/ Dispatch \/ Complete \/ Release \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected == Len(queue) <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    CAP = 2
    MaxTasks = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm feeds imagery-analysis tasks into a central dispatch queue that has strictly bounded capacity. Drones submit new tasks, but the queue applies backpressure: a submission is only accepted when there is free room, otherwise the drone must hold the frame and try again later. A pool of ground-station workers pulls tasks from the head of the queue and processes them one at a time. A worker may be slow but is never considered failed: while holding a task it can take arbitrarily long, and if it decides it cannot keep up it releases the task back into the queue, but only when there is still room so the queue is never overfilled by a release either. Completed tasks are recorded as done and free the worker again. New tasks stop being created once the mission's task budget is reached, keeping the run finite; once the budget is spent and every worker is idle with an empty queue, the swarm simply idles. The dispatcher and the release path both re-check remaining room before touching the queue.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of tasks waiting in the dispatch queue never exceeds the queue's fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m0p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Trains, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, pending, committed

vars == <<epoch, pending, committed>>

InSeq(x, s) == \E i \in DOMAIN s : s[i] = x

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ committed = <<>>

Prepare ==
    /\ \E t \in Trains :
         /\ ~InSeq(t, committed)
         /\ [train |-> t, obs |-> epoch] \notin pending
         /\ pending' = pending \cup {[train |-> t, obs |-> epoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, committed>>

Commit ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E r \in pending :
         /\ r.obs = epoch
         /\ ~InSeq(r.train, committed)
         /\ committed' = Append(committed, r.train)
         /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
         /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ TRUE

Discard ==
    /\ \E r \in pending :
         /\ r.obs # epoch
         /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, committed>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A r \in pending : r.obs # epoch
    /\ (\A t \in Trains : InSeq(t, committed)) \/ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Prepare \/ Commit \/ Discard \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommittedAtMostOnce == \A i, j \in DOMAIN committed : committed[i] = committed[j] => i = j
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Trains = {t1, t2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CommittedAtMostOnce
nl:
A subway signalling block system dispatches trains through a shared interlocking using optimistic locking. Each dispatch request carries the epoch value the train observed when it prepared, and the interlocking only commits a dispatch if that observed epoch still matches the current epoch; otherwise the request is stale and the train must retry with a fresh observation. Requests arrive over an unreliable link and may be applied in any order, so a batch of prepared requests sits in a pending pool and the interlocking picks any one to try. Committing a dispatch is an irreversible movement authority that consumes the train's turn and stamps it into the committed sequence, and it must never be granted twice to the same train. A stale request can be discarded so the train re-prepares. Each successful commit advances the epoch, invalidating every other observation that was made against the old epoch. When no request can make progress the interlocking idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No train is ever granted a committed movement authority more than once.

---- MODULE W4Od17m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bags, CAP

VARIABLES queue, loaded, arrived, crashed

vars == <<queue, loaded, arrived, crashed>>

InSeq(x, s) == \E i \in DOMAIN s : s[i] = x

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ loaded = <<>>
    /\ arrived = {}
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Arrive ==
    /\ \E b \in Bags :
         /\ b \notin arrived
         /\ Len(queue) < CAP
         /\ queue' = Append(queue, b)
         /\ arrived' = arrived \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, crashed>>

Load ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ ~InSeq(Head(queue), loaded)
    /\ loaded' = Append(loaded, Head(queue))
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<arrived, crashed>>

Recirculate ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ Len(queue) < CAP
    /\ ~InSeq(Head(queue), loaded)
    /\ queue' = Append(Tail(queue), Head(queue))
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loaded, arrived, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, loaded, arrived>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ (crashed \/ (Len(queue) = 0 /\ arrived = Bags))
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Arrive \/ Load \/ Recirculate \/ Crash \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LoadedAtMostOnce == \A i, j \in DOMAIN loaded : loaded[i] = loaded[j] => i = j
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bags = {b1, b2, b3}
    CAP = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadedAtMostOnce
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags into a bounded scanning queue and then loads each scanned bag onto a departure cart. New bags may only join the queue while there is free room; when the queue is full the belt applies backpressure and the bag waits upstream. A router pulls the bag at the head of the queue and loads it onto a cart, an irreversible physical commit that must never be repeated for the same bag. A bag that is diverted for a manual re-check can be recirculated back into the queue, but only if it has not yet been loaded and only if the queue has room. One router can crash silently: it simply stops loading bags with no error signal, after which no further loads occur. Once every bag has either been loaded or the system has gone quiet, the belt idles. The load path always checks that the bag has not already been committed before loading it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No bag is ever loaded onto a departure cart more than once.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, CAP

VARIABLES buffer, active, complete, crashed

vars == <<buffer, active, complete, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ buffer = {}
    /\ active = {}
    /\ complete = {}
    /\ crashed = FALSE

Raise ==
    /\ Cardinality(buffer) < CAP
    /\ \E m \in Machines :
         /\ m \notin buffer
         /\ m \notin active
         /\ m \notin complete
         /\ buffer' = buffer \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, complete, crashed>>

Claim ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ \E m \in buffer :
         /\ buffer' = buffer \ {m}
         /\ active' = active \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<complete, crashed>>

Finish ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ \E m \in active :
         /\ active' = active \ {m}
         /\ complete' = complete \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<buffer, crashed>>

Cancel ==
    /\ \E m \in buffer :
         buffer' = buffer \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<active, complete, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ ~crashed
    /\ crashed' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<buffer, active, complete>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ buffer = {}
    /\ (crashed \/ active = {})
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Raise \/ Claim \/ Finish \/ Cancel \/ Crash \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BufferWithinCapacity == Cardinality(buffer) <= CAP
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
    CAP = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BufferWithinCapacity
nl:
A vending machine network collects restock jobs into a shared dispatch buffer of strictly bounded size. A machine may raise a restock job only when the buffer has free room; otherwise the request is held back as backpressure. A field technician node claims a job from the buffer and moves it into active servicing, and later marks it complete. One technician node can crash silently: it stops claiming and completing jobs with no notice, so any job it was about to take simply stays in the buffer. A machine that has raised a job may cancel it while it is still waiting, freeing a buffer slot. The number of jobs sitting in the dispatch buffer must never exceed the buffer's fixed size, and every path that adds to the buffer re-checks the remaining room first. When no machine can raise a job and the buffer is drained, the network idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of restock jobs held in the dispatch buffer never exceeds the buffer's fixed size.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p1t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets, TLC

CONSTANTS Instr, CAP, Opening

Amt == (1 :> 5) @@ (2 :> 3) @@ (3 :> 2)

RECURSIVE SumAmt(_)
SumAmt(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
             ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN Amt[x] + SumAmt(S \ {x})

VARIABLES pending, applied, bounced, balance

vars == <<pending, applied, bounced, balance>>

Untouched == Instr \ (pending \cup applied \cup bounced)

Init ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ bounced = {}
    /\ balance = Opening

Admit ==
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < CAP
    /\ \E x \in Untouched :
         pending' = pending \cup {x}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, bounced, balance>>

Post ==
    /\ \E x \in pending :
         /\ balance' = balance + Amt[x]
         /\ applied' = applied \cup {x}
         /\ pending' = pending \ {x}
    /\ UNCHANGED bounced

Bounce ==
    /\ Cardinality(pending) >= CAP
    /\ \E x \in Untouched :
         bounced' = bounced \cup {x}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, applied, balance>>

Rebook ==
    /\ Cardinality(pending) < CAP
    /\ \E x \in bounced :
         /\ pending' = pending \cup {x}
         /\ bounced' = bounced \ {x}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, balance>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ (Untouched = {} \/ Cardinality(pending) >= CAP)
    /\ bounced = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Admit \/ Post \/ Bounce \/ Rebook \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == balance = Opening + SumAmt(applied)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instr = {1, 2, 3}
    CAP = 2
    Opening = 10
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch applies a stream of settlement instructions to a shared clearing balance. Instructions are admitted into a bounded pending pool; while the pool is full the gateway applies backpressure and refuses new admissions until room frees. Because instructions arrive over several links they may be applied in any order, so the settlement engine picks any admitted instruction to post next. Posting an instruction adds its signed amount to the shared balance and records the instruction as applied, and the accounting rule is that the balance must always equal the opening balance plus the total of every amount that has been applied, so no update is ever silently dropped or clobbered by a concurrent post. When the pending pool is full an un-admitted instruction may be bounced aside, and a bounced instruction may later be re-booked into the pool once capacity is available. Every instruction is admitted at most once. When nothing remains to admit or post, the batch idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared clearing balance always equals the opening balance plus the sum of the amounts of all instructions that have been applied.

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Locks, Controllers

VARIABLES epoch, cLog, pending

vars == <<epoch, cLog, pending>>

SealedLocks == { cLog[i].lock : i \in DOMAIN cLog }

Init ==
    /\ epoch = [l \in Locks |-> 0]
    /\ cLog = <<>>
    /\ pending = {}

Prepare ==
    /\ \E c \in Controllers, l \in Locks :
         /\ l \notin SealedLocks
         /\ [ctrl |-> c, lock |-> l, obs |-> epoch[l]] \notin pending
         /\ pending' = pending \cup {[ctrl |-> c, lock |-> l, obs |-> epoch[l]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cLog>>

Commission ==
    /\ \E r \in pending :
         /\ r.obs = epoch[r.lock]
         /\ r.lock \notin SealedLocks
         /\ cLog' = Append(cLog, [lock |-> r.lock, ctrl |-> r.ctrl])
         /\ epoch' = [epoch EXCEPT ![r.lock] = @ + 1]
         /\ pending' = pending \ {r}

Retract ==
    /\ \E r \in pending :
         /\ r.obs # epoch[r.lock]
         /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cLog>>

Abort ==
    /\ \E c \in Controllers :
         /\ \E r \in pending : r.ctrl = c
         /\ pending' = { r \in pending : r.ctrl # c }
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, cLog>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A r \in pending : r.obs # epoch[r.lock]
    /\ (Locks \subseteq SealedLocks) \/ pending = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Prepare \/ Commission \/ Retract \/ Abort \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CommissionedAtMostOnce ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN cLog : cLog[i].lock = cLog[j].lock => i = j
====
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network lets two independent controller instances commission locks out of one shared pool. Commissioning a lock burns its factory pairing and is irreversible, so a given lock must be commissioned exactly once even though both controllers race for the same pool. Each controller prepares a commissioning request by reading the lock's current pairing epoch; it then submits the request, and the pool only accepts it if the observed epoch still matches the lock's live epoch, otherwise the request is stale and the controller must re-prepare. A successful commission stamps the lock and controller into the commissioning log and advances that lock's epoch, invalidating every other outstanding request against it. A controller may abort, dropping all of its own prepared requests. Because both controllers share the pool, optimistic epoch checking is what stops the two from both commissioning the same lock. When no request can commit, the network idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No lock in the shared pool is ever commissioned more than once.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Feeders = {1, 2, 3}
    CAP = 2
    Total = 9
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LoadConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed set of feeders, each carrying a fixed amount of load, and two independent shedder instances draw shed-requests from one shared pool. A feeder starts online. To shed it, the controller first moves it into a bounded pending pool, but only while that pool has free room, applying backpressure when it is full. From the pending pool either shedder instance A or shedder instance B may actually trip the feeder, moving it into that instance's shed set. A tripped feeder can later be restored back online. The grid's invariant is conservation: no load is ever created or destroyed, so the load that is online, plus the load queued pending, plus the load shed by instance A, plus the load shed by instance B, always sums to the fixed grid total. Every transition simply moves a feeder from one bucket to another. When nothing more can move, the shedder idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The total load across the online, pending, A-shed, and B-shed buckets always equals the fixed grid total.

---- MODULE W4Od5m3p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Players, Admin

VARIABLES leader, inCS, alive, waiting, matched

vars == <<leader, inCS, alive, waiting, matched>>

NONE == "NoLeader"

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ alive = Nodes
    /\ waiting = Players
    /\ matched = {}

Elect ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ \E n \in alive :
         leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, alive, waiting, matched>>

EnterAndAssign ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ waiting # {}
    /\ \E p \in waiting :
         /\ matched' = matched \cup {p}
         /\ waiting' = waiting \ {p}
    /\ inCS' = {leader}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive>>

Leave ==
    /\ inCS # {}
    /\ inCS' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, alive, waiting, matched>>

Fail ==
    /\ leader # NONE
    /\ leader \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {leader}
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {leader}
    /\ leader' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, matched>>

Recover ==
    /\ \E n \in Nodes :
         /\ n \notin alive
         /\ alive' = alive \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, inCS, waiting, matched>>

AdminOverride ==
    /\ \E n \in alive :
         leader' = n
    /\ inCS' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, waiting, matched>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ alive = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Elect \/ EnterAndAssign \/ Leave \/ Fail \/ Recover \/ AdminOverride \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CriticalSectionExclusive == \A n1, n2 \in inCS : n1 = n2
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    Players = {p1, p2}
    Admin = adm
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CriticalSectionExclusive
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker runs on a cluster of nodes, but only the elected leader may write to the shared match ledger, which is the critical resource. When there is no leader, any live node can be elected. The leader enters the critical section to pull a waiting player from the queue and commit them into a match, then leaves. A leader can fail over: it crashes, loses liveness, and leadership is vacated, and any occupancy of the critical section by that crashed node is cleared. A crashed node may later recover and rejoin as a candidate. A privileged admin override can forcibly install any live node as leader; because this pre-empts whoever was there, the override first evicts every node from the critical section so no two nodes are ever writing at once. The whole point is that at most one node is inside the critical section at any instant. When every node has crashed the cluster idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time are two different nodes simultaneously inside the match-ledger critical section.

CONSTANTS
    Instr = {1, 2, 3}
    CAP = 2
    Opening = 20
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch posts settlement instructions to a shared clearing balance. Instructions are admitted into a bounded pending pool under backpressure: no admission while the pool is full. The settlement engine posts any admitted instruction, adding its signed amount to the balance and recording it as applied. A full pool may bounce an un-admitted instruction aside. SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared clearing balance always equals the opening balance plus the sum of the amounts of all applied instructions.

---- MODULE W4Od14m0p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES authEpoch, droneEpoch, acting, served

vars == <<authEpoch, droneEpoch, acting, served>>

Init ==
    /\ authEpoch = 0
    /\ droneEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ served = {}

Refresh ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones :
         /\ droneEpoch[d] # authEpoch
         /\ droneEpoch' = [droneEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = authEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, acting, served>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ authEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ authEpoch' = authEpoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<droneEpoch, acting, served>>

StartUpload ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones :
         /\ droneEpoch[d] = authEpoch
         /\ d \notin acting
         /\ d \notin served
         /\ acting' = acting \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, droneEpoch, served>>

FinishUpload ==
    /\ \E d \in acting :
         /\ acting' = acting \ {d}
         /\ served' = served \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<authEpoch, droneEpoch>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ authEpoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ \A d \in Drones : droneEpoch[d] = authEpoch => d \in served
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Refresh \/ Reconfigure \/ StartUpload \/ FinishUpload \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleActor == \A d \in acting : droneEpoch[d] = authEpoch
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleActor
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm authorizes drones to upload imagery only while they hold the current mission epoch. Each drone caches the epoch it last observed; a drone that has fallen behind is slow, not failed, and simply holds a stale epoch until it refreshes. A drone may begin an upload action only if its cached epoch matches the swarm's live authority epoch, an optimistic check that rejects any stale participant. The ground station can reconfigure the mission, advancing the authority epoch and instantly invalidating every drone that has not refreshed. A slow drone refreshes by re-reading the live epoch, after which it is authorized again. A drone that has begun an upload later finishes it and moves to the served set. The safety rule is that no drone is ever mid-upload while holding a stale epoch. When no drone can start, refresh, or finish, the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drone currently performing an upload holds an epoch equal to the swarm's live authority epoch.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m4p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Rx, Slots, CAP

VARIABLES queue, allocLog, usedSlots, dispensed

vars == <<queue, allocLog, usedSlots, dispensed>>

InSeq(x, s) == \E i \in DOMAIN s : s[i] = x
BoundRx == { allocLog[i].rx : i \in DOMAIN allocLog }

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ allocLog = <<>>
    /\ usedSlots = {}
    /\ dispensed = {}

Enqueue ==
    /\ Len(queue) < CAP
    /\ \E r \in Rx :
         /\ ~InSeq(r, queue)
         /\ r \notin BoundRx
         /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocLog, usedSlots, dispensed>>

AllocRobot1 ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
         /\ s \notin usedSlots
         /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, [rx |-> Head(queue), slot |-> s])
         /\ usedSlots' = usedSlots \cup {s}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED dispensed

AllocRobot2 ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ \E s \in Slots :
         /\ s \notin usedSlots
         /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, [rx |-> Head(queue), slot |-> s])
         /\ usedSlots' = usedSlots \cup {s}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED dispensed

PickUp ==
    /\ \E i \in DOMAIN allocLog :
         /\ allocLog[i].rx \notin dispensed
         /\ dispensed' = dispensed \cup {allocLog[i].rx}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, allocLog, usedSlots>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ usedSlots = Slots
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Enqueue \/ AllocRobot1 \/ AllocRobot2 \/ PickUp \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN allocLog : allocLog[i].slot = allocLog[j].slot => i = j
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Rx = {r1, r2, r3}
    Slots = {s1, s2}
    CAP = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser feeds prescriptions into a bounded intake queue and two independent dispensing robots draw from that one shared queue. A prescription only joins the queue when there is free room; a full queue applies backpressure. Each robot takes the prescription at the head of the queue and binds it to a single-use pickup slot, appending the prescription-and-slot pairing to the dispatch log and marking that slot used. A slot may only be bound while it is still unused, so the same slot is never allocated twice even with both robots racing for the shared pool. A prescription that has been bound to a slot is later picked up and marked dispensed. The dispenser's integrity rule is that no pickup slot ever appears in the dispatch log for two different bindings. When every slot has been consumed, the dispenser idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No pickup slot is ever allocated to more than one prescription binding in the dispatch log.

---- MODULE W4Od4m7p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, CAP

VARIABLES count, onBelt, ops, left

    /\ onBelt = {}
    /\ ops = {}
    /\ left = {}

ProposeEnter ==
    /\ count < CAP
    /\ \E c \in Cars :
         /\ c \notin onBelt
         /\ c \notin left
         /\ [car |-> c, kind |-> "in", expect |-> count] \notin ops
         /\ ops' = ops \cup {[car |-> c, kind |-> "in", expect |-> count]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, onBelt, left>>

ProposeExit ==
    /\ \E c \in onBelt :
         /\ [car |-> c, kind |-> "out", expect |-> count] \notin ops
         /\ ops' = ops \cup {[car |-> c, kind |-> "out", expect |-> count]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, onBelt, left>>

ApplyEnter ==
    /\ \E o \in ops :
         /\ o.kind = "in"
         /\ o.expect = count
         /\ count' = count + 1
         /\ onBelt' = onBelt \cup {o.car}
         /\ ops' = { p \in ops : p.car # o.car }
    /\ UNCHANGED left

ApplyExit ==
    /\ \E o \in ops :
         /\ o.kind = "out"
         /\ o.expect = count
         /\ count' = count - 1
         /\ onBelt' = onBelt \ {o.car}
         /\ left' = left \cup {o.car}
         /\ ops' = { p \in ops : p.car # o.car }

         /\ o.expect # count
         /\ ops' = ops \ {o}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, onBelt, left>>

    /\ onBelt = {}
    /\ count = CAP \/ (\A c \in Cars : c \in left)

CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    CAP = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OccupancyWithinCapacity
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line uses a single compare-and-swap occupancy register to keep the number of cars on the belt within a fixed capacity. A car wanting to enter reads the register value and, only if it is below capacity, prepares a CAS operation that expects that value and would increment it. A car wanting to leave prepares a CAS that expects the current value and would decrement it. Prepared operations sit in a pool and, because sensors report out of order, the controller applies them in any order. An operation is only applied if the register still equals the value the operation expected; otherwise the operation is stale and is dropped so the car can re-prepare. Applying an entry op puts the car on the belt and bumps the register up; applying an exit op removes the car and bumps it down. Because entry ops are only prepared while the register reads below capacity and CAS re-checks that exact value, occupancy never exceeds capacity. When no operation can be prepared or applied, the line idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the conveyor belt never exceeds the fixed capacity.

CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {a1, a2, a3}
    CAP = 2
    Fleet = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator moves a fixed set of aircraft through a pipeline of buckets. Every aircraft begins waiting. To be sequenced it is moved into a bounded ready queue, but only while that queue has free room, applying backpressure when it is full. The allocator clears a queued aircraft onto the runway, and a cleared aircraft eventually departs. The allocator process can crash silently: it simply stops clearing aircraft, with no signal, so queued aircraft accumulate but nothing is ever fabricated or lost. The conservation rule is that every aircraft is always in exactly one bucket, so the total count across waiting, queued, cleared, and departed always equals the fixed number of aircraft. ---- MODULE W4Od13m7p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Buyers, Slots

VARIABLES reg, allocLog, props

vars == <<reg, allocLog, props>>

TAKEN == "taken"
FREEV == "free"
BoundBuyers == { allocLog[i].buyer : i \in DOMAIN allocLog }

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Slots |-> FREEV]
    /\ allocLog = <<>>
    /\ props = {}

Propose ==
    /\ \E b \in Buyers, s \in Slots :
         /\ b \notin BoundBuyers
         /\ [buyer |-> b, slot |-> s] \notin props
         /\ props' = props \cup {[buyer |-> b, slot |-> s]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, allocLog>>

CommitCAS ==
    /\ \E p \in props :
         /\ reg[p.slot] = FREEV
         /\ p.buyer \notin BoundBuyers
         /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![p.slot] = TAKEN]
         /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, [buyer |-> p.buyer, slot |-> p.slot])
         /\ props' = props \ {p}

DropStale ==
    /\ \E p \in props :
         /\ reg[p.slot] # FREEV
         /\ props' = props \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, allocLog>>

AdminForceClaim ==
    /\ \E b \in Buyers, s \in Slots :
         /\ reg[s] = FREEV
         /\ b \notin BoundBuyers
         /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = TAKEN]
         /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, [buyer |-> b, slot |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED props

Quiesce ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : reg[s] = TAKEN
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Propose \/ CommitCAS \/ DropStale \/ AdminForceClaim \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN allocLog : allocLog[i].slot = allocLog[j].slot => i = j
====
nl:
A vending machine network dispenses items out of single-use slots guarded by a per-slot compare-and-swap register that reads free or taken. A buyer proposes a claim on a slot; the proposal only commits if the slot's register still reads free at commit time, at which point the register flips to taken and the buyer-slot binding is appended to the allocation log. If the register no longer reads free the proposal is stale and is dropped so the buyer can try another slot. A privileged operator override can force-claim any still-free slot directly for a priority buyer, also flipping the register and appending to the log. Both the compare-and-swap commit and the operator override only ever act on a slot whose register reads free, so a slot is never bound to two different buyers. Each buyer is bound at most once. When every slot has been taken the network idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No vending slot ever appears in the allocation log bound to two different buyers.

CONSTANTS
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Changes = {p1, p2}
    Quorum = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CounterMatchesCommits
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line commits configuration changes to a shared cycle counter only through quorum voting. Each pending change is opened for a vote; the controller nodes cast votes for the currently open change, and the change commits only once a quorum of votes has been gathered, at which point the counter is bumped and the change is recorded as committed. One controller node can crash silently: it simply stops casting votes, but since the quorum is a strict majority the remaining nodes can still reach it, so no committed change is ever lost or double-counted. The rule is that the counter always equals the number of changes that have committed. A committed change closes the vote so the next one can open. When every change has committed and no vote is open, the line idles.

    /\ committed = {}

         /\ n \notin committed
         /\ coarse' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, counter, staged, committed, cap>>

AcquireFine ==
    /\ fine = NONE
    /\ coarse # NONE
    /\ fine' = coarse
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, counter, staged, committed, cap>>

ReadStage ==
    /\ fine # NONE
    /\ staged[fine] = 0 - 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![fine] = counter]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, counter, committed, cap>>

    /\ fine # NONE
    /\ staged[fine] >= 0
    /\ fine \notin committed
    /\ counter < cap
    /\ counter' = staged[fine] + 1
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {fine}
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![fine] = 0 - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, cap>>

    /\ coarse # NONE
    /\ coarse' = NONE
    /\ fine' = NONE
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![coarse] = 0 - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<counter, committed, cap>>

Each node contributes at most once. Because the operator can always readjust the cap, the matchmaker never gets stuck.

nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants a controller a time-bounded lease over the active runway. A lease is granted only when no live lease exists, and it carries an expiry a fixed horizon ahead of the current clock; past that clock value the lease is dead. Only the holder of a live lease may issue a takeoff clearance to an aircraft, which is an irreversible commit that must happen at most once per aircraft. The clock advances in ticks. A holder can crash silently: it stops issuing clearances with no notice, but its lease still lapses at expiry so another controller can take over. Because grants require the aircraft to be uncleared, no aircraft is ever cleared twice. When every aircraft has been cleared and the clock has run out, the tower idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No aircraft is ever issued a takeoff clearance more than once.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m9p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Dispensers, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, nodeEpoch, head

vars == <<epoch, nodeEpoch, head>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ nodeEpoch = [d \in Dispensers |-> 0]
    /\ head = {}

Refresh ==
    /\ \E d \in Dispensers :
         /\ nodeEpoch[d] # epoch
         /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, head>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ head = {}
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nodeEpoch, head>>

Enter ==
    /\ head = {}
    /\ \E d \in Dispensers :
         /\ nodeEpoch[d] = epoch
         /\ head' = {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch>>

Leave ==
    /\ head # {}
    /\ head' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch>>

AdminOverride ==
    /\ \E d \in Dispensers :
         head' = {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch>>

Next == Refresh \/ Reconfigure \/ Enter \/ Leave \/ AdminOverride

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

HeadExclusive == \A a, b \in head : a = b
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Dispensers = {h1, h2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT HeadExclusive
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser network guards a single shared dispensing head, the critical resource, with epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Each dispenser node caches the configuration epoch it last saw. The network can reconfigure, advancing the epoch, but only while the dispensing head is unoccupied, so no reconfiguration ever strands a node inside the critical section. A node may enter the critical section only when the head is free and the node's cached epoch matches the live epoch. A slow node refreshes its cached epoch to catch up. The occupant leaves when done. A privileged pharmacy administrator override can forcibly seize the head for any node, which evicts whoever was there so that the head is still held by exactly one node. The whole point is that the dispensing head is never held by two nodes at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time are two different dispenser nodes simultaneously holding the shared dispensing head.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m9p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Drones, SurveySlots, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, droneEpoch, allocLog, usedSlots, crashed

vars == <<epoch, droneEpoch, allocLog, usedSlots, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ droneEpoch = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ allocLog = <<>>
    /\ usedSlots = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Refresh ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones :
         /\ droneEpoch[d] # epoch
         /\ droneEpoch' = [droneEpoch EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, allocLog, usedSlots, crashed>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<droneEpoch, allocLog, usedSlots, crashed>>

Allocate ==
    /\ \E d \in Drones, s \in SurveySlots :
         /\ d \notin crashed
         /\ droneEpoch[d] = epoch
         /\ s \notin usedSlots
         /\ allocLog' = Append(allocLog, [drone |-> d, slot |-> s])
         /\ usedSlots' = usedSlots \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, droneEpoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E d \in Drones : crashed' = {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, droneEpoch, allocLog, usedSlots>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ usedSlots = SurveySlots
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Refresh \/ Reconfigure \/ Allocate \/ Crash \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN allocLog : allocLog[i].slot = allocLog[j].slot => i = j
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    SurveySlots = {z1, z2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm allocates single-use survey slots under epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Each drone caches the mission epoch it last observed. The ground station can reconfigure the mission, advancing the epoch and invalidating every drone that has not refreshed. A drone may allocate a survey slot only if its cached epoch matches the live epoch and the slot is still unallocated; the allocation is appended to the assignment log and the slot is marked used. A slow drone refreshes to the live epoch to become eligible again. One drone can crash silently, ceasing to allocate with no notice. The integrity rule is that no survey slot ever appears in the assignment log for two different allocations. When every slot has been allocated the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No survey slot is ever allocated to more than one drone in the assignment log.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m9p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, craneEpoch, acting, done, crashed

vars == <<epoch, craneEpoch, acting, done, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ craneEpoch = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ done = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Refresh ==
    /\ \E c \in Cranes :
         /\ craneEpoch[c] # epoch
         /\ craneEpoch' = [craneEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, acting, done, crashed>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<craneEpoch, acting, done, crashed>>

StartMove ==
    /\ \E c \in Cranes :
         /\ c \notin crashed
         /\ craneEpoch[c] = epoch
         /\ c \notin acting
         /\ c \notin done
         /\ acting' = acting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, craneEpoch, done, crashed>>

FinishMove ==
    /\ \E c \in acting :
         /\ acting' = acting \ {c}
         /\ done' = done \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, craneEpoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E c \in Cranes : crashed' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, craneEpoch, acting, done>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ \A c \in Cranes : c \in done \/ c \in crashed
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Refresh \/ Reconfigure \/ StartMove \/ FinishMove \/ Crash \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleActor == \A c \in acting : craneEpoch[c] = epoch
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {k1, k2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleActor
nl:
A container-ship crane yard authorizes cranes to execute moves only under the current configuration epoch. Each crane caches the epoch it last observed. The yard controller can reconfigure, advancing the epoch, but only while no crane is mid-move, so a reconfiguration never leaves a crane executing under a stale authorization. A crane may begin a move only if its cached epoch matches the live epoch, which rejects any stale or unauthorized crane. A slow crane refreshes its epoch to become authorized again. A crane that has begun a move later finishes it and is recorded done. One crane can crash silently, ceasing to move with no notice. The safety rule is that every crane currently executing a move holds an epoch equal to the live authorization epoch. When the epoch is maxed out and every crane is done or crashed, the yard idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane currently executing a move holds an epoch equal to the yard's live authorization epoch.

---- MODULE W4Od8m9p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RegNodes, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, nodeEpoch, lock, registered, crashed

vars == <<epoch, nodeEpoch, lock, registered, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ nodeEpoch = [n \in RegNodes |-> 0]
    /\ lock = {}
    /\ registered = {}
    /\ crashed = {}

Refresh ==
    /\ \E n \in RegNodes :
         /\ nodeEpoch[n] # epoch
         /\ nodeEpoch' = [nodeEpoch EXCEPT ![n] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, lock, registered, crashed>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ lock = {}
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<nodeEpoch, lock, registered, crashed>>

Enter ==
    /\ lock = {}
    /\ \E n \in RegNodes :
         /\ n \notin crashed
         /\ n \notin registered
         /\ nodeEpoch[n] = epoch
         /\ lock' = {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch, registered, crashed>>

Leave ==
    /\ \E n \in lock :
         /\ registered' = registered \cup {n}
         /\ lock' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch, crashed>>

Crash ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E n \in RegNodes : crashed' = {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, nodeEpoch, lock, registered>>

Quiesce ==
    /\ epoch = MaxEpoch
    /\ lock = {}
    /\ \A n \in RegNodes : n \in registered \/ n \in crashed
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next == Refresh \/ Reconfigure \/ Enter \/ Leave \/ Crash \/ Quiesce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LockExclusive == \A a, b \in lock : a = b
====

    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LockExclusive
nl:
A university course-registration system guards the write lock on a shared roster, the critical resource, with epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Each registration node caches the epoch it last observed. The registrar can reconfigure, advancing the epoch, but only while the roster lock is free, so no reconfiguration ever strands a node inside the critical section. A node may enter the critical section to commit a registration only if the lock is free, its cached epoch matches the live epoch, and it has not already registered. A slow node refreshes its cached epoch to catch up. Leaving the critical section commits the node's registration. One node can crash silently, ceasing to participate with no notice. The invariant is that the roster write lock is never held by two nodes at once. When the epoch is maxed out and every node is registered or crashed, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At no time are two different registration nodes simultaneously holding the roster write lock.
